publication_year_note: Journal volume/article header prints 'Environ Monit Assess (2022) 194:912' and history prints 'Received: 22 March 2022 / Accepted: 7 October 2022 / Published online: 18 October 2022' (both 2022).
rationale: This mixed-methods case study of three rural communities in Chiapas, Mexico (N = 90 convenience-sampled household questionnaires, 3 focus groups, and n = 153 household water-quality samples) reports only descriptive statistics (frequencies/percentages in Figs. 2-3; medians, SDs, and min/max of physicochemical/microbiological water-quality indicators in Tables 2-3), an exploratory principal component analysis biplot (53% variance explained across two components; Fig. 4) without hypothesis tests, and qualitative coding of community water management barriers and bridges (Table 4). No inferential statistical tests, regression estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, test statistics, or p-values are reported anywhere in the text. Flagging quantitative synthesis eligibility is therefore overstated.
